intro: Lesson 19. Read each word slowly, pointing with your finger. Only the Arabic is the Qur'an; the English is a translation of its meaning.

arabic.text: لَآ أُقْسِمُ بِهَٰذَا ٱلْبَلَدِ (١) وَأَنتَ حِلٌّۢ بِهَٰذَا ٱلْبَلَدِ (٢) وَوَالِدٍۢ وَمَا وَلَدَ (٣) لَقَدْ خَلَقْنَا ٱلْإِنسَٰنَ فِى كَبَدٍ (٤) أَيَحْسَبُ أَن لَّن يَقْدِرَ عَلَيْهِ أَحَدٌۭ (٥) يَقُولُ أَهْلَكْتُ مَالًۭا لُّبَدًا (٦) أَيَحْسَبُ أَن لَّمْ يَرَهُۥٓ أَحَدٌ (٧)

head: Ayah
Translation of the meaning (Saheeh International)
rows: I swear by this city, Makkah -
And you, [O Muhammad], are free of restriction in this city -
And [by] the father and that which was born [of him],
We have certainly created man into hardship.
Does he think that never will anyone overcome him?
He says, "I have spent wealth in abundance."
Does he think that no one has seen him?

questions.q: Chunk and link Al-Balad 90:1-7 together, ayah by ayah.
questions.a: The class recites 90:1-7 together without the mushaf.

questions.q: «لَآ أُقْسِمُ» (90:1): the alif is stretched for ...
Listening rota: today's group recites 90:1-7 to the teacher, one by one. Everyone else: 3-3-link the same ayat, then tick the revision log.
questions.a: Pupil recites with no help; the teacher marks hifdh and tajweed on the rubric and gives one target.

questions.q: On the pupil PDF, circle the madd letters in 90:6.
In one sentence: what is the man in 90:6 boasting about?
questions.a: He boasts that he has spent a great deal of wealth, as if that makes him great.

questions.q: In 90:7 Allah asks: 'Does he think that ...
questions.a: A) no one has seen him?. 90:7: 'Does he think that no one has seen him?' Allah sees how we spend our wealth.

questions.q: Al-Balad 90:4: «لَقَدْ خَلَقْنَا ...» Which word comes next?
Think again: Allah says He created people 'into hardship' (90:4). Why might struggle and effort be part of every life?
questions.a: Life is a test: we work, study and are patient. Effort for Allah's sake is rewarded, and struggles make us stronger.
